original.description: This activity will evaluate the technical and commercial feasibility of developing a standardised and interoperable set of Flat Panel User Terminal (UT) building blocks and internal interfaces, able to be reused in end user equipment designed for deployment across a broad range of market sectors and network types.The objective is to support the creation of a scalable, industrialised and costcompetitive ecosystem for flat panel user terminals in the ESA Member States by enabling economies of scale through open architectures and harmonised specifications.The activity will also identify standardised FPA terminal profiles (classes'), defining their RFperformance characteristics and associated validation and certification methodologies, to facilitate objective performance assessment and enable fair and interoperable competition among vendors.

original.description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of resilient PNT payload technologies based on digital and AI-enabled architectures. The study will investigate reconfigurable, software-defined payloads capable of characterizing and adapting to dynamic, congested or impaired RF environments.The activity will address the full signal chain, from generation to transmission, including onboard processing and AI-based techniques. A digital twin environment is also foreseen to be developed to support validation andperformance assessment.The objective is to mature concept and associated key payload technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible, flight-representative architecture for next-generation PNT systems.

original.description: The objective(s) of this activity are the following:a) Design and implement an end-to-end Space Segment testbed that can constitute a security reference architecture, including a number of cyber security building blocks.b) Perform a security assessment and verification of the implemented security measures using the selected cyber security building blocks.c) Identify potential security enhancements, that can constitute candidates for further technical developments into products.The targeted current Technology ReadinessLevel (TRL) of this activity is 4 [RD1].WORK TO BE PERFORMED1 Work LogicThe work will be organised in two phases and the following tasks:Phase 1: Definition of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 1: State-of-the-art survey of mission scenarios, security threats, relevant legislations and regulations and security technologiesoTask 2: Consolidationof Space Segment modular security reference architecture, including identification of required cyber security building blocks andspecification of system Space Segment security requirements.oTask 3: Specification of Space Segment testbed requirements (including incorporated cyber security building blocks), design and implementation and test planningPhase 2: Development, implementation and testing of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 4: Development of the Space Segment testbedoTask 5: Space Segment Testbed Testing, Security Assessment and Vulnerability MitigationoTask 6: Lessons learnt and proposed roadmap for further (other than [RD16] building blocks development (including high level specifications)Note that phase 2 will be authorised to implement the agreed building blocks, subject to a successful Phase 1 and acceptance of a proposal for the conversion of the Phase 2 price from ceilingprice to Firm Fixed Price.

This tender is one of two being implemented as part of the 'Support to Disaster Risk Reduction through Earth Observation and Climate Services in South Asia' (SADRR) initiative (2026-2029). The initiative is being carried out in partnership with the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and is funded by the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA) as part of the Global Gateway initiative.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 54 Mbaud DVB-S2 and 5G NR demodulator on a low-end Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) or Central Processing Unit (CPU).Targeted Improvements: Enabling a 54 Mbaud software defined radio for low end platforms not existing today in ESA Member States.Description: Previous projects have demonstrated that carriers of equivalent bandwidth can be demodulated in software on x86 server-level CPUs. Also, by using high-performance GPUs and parallel processing, bandwidths of hundreds of MHz or even many GHz could be demodulated. To date, a low-cost GPU or CPU-based demodulation solution with typical consumer terminal performance have not been developed. Such technology would allow field-upgradable terminals that can enable the deployment of new waveforms without expensive hardware swaps in the middle of the life of the system.This activity will develop and test a software-based demodulator running in a consumer GPU as found in a games console or a PC graphics card or a low-end CPU (Intel Core i3 or equivalent), with a throughput equivalent to a TV receiver or a consumer satellite broadband terminal. Superior demodulation algorithms than those in common open-source Software Defined Radio (SDR) toolkits will be studied and further developed and implemented.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall implement and test a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on one of the hardware platforms described above. The DVB-S2/X demodulator software will be tested against a hardware modulator or dedicated test equipment in the relevant environment to ensure the baud rate is met and fully compliant with as a minimum theDVB-S2 specification. Phase 1 deliverable will be a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on a low-end CPU or GPU platform. Budget is up to 700 kEuro.- Phase 2 shall implement and test in the relevant environment 5G-NR waveform or other proprietary waveform development on the hardware platform delivered by Phase 1.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: The objective of this activity is to design, implement and evaluate different types of satellite system architectural models aimed at dynamically focusing available resources on coverage gaps in terrestrial 4G and 5G networks.Targeted Improvements:Achieving national regulator coverage and service objectives for direct-to-device services and enabling twice as efficient satellite resourcespooling over the service area.Description: Today there are coverage gaps of the terrestrial telecommunication system despite initiatives from non-European industries to provide supplementary coverage from space. Concentrating satellite connectivity exclusively on coverage gap areas (including low service areas) rather than aiming for satellite connectivity over a broad coverage has the potential to maximize the efficiency of the satellite system. It could offer an increased throughput which translates in reduced deployment costs per bit and higher quality of service for end users. Moreover, this approach could enable flexible resources allocation based on the population density as well as step up and step down of terrestrial connectivity services.This activity will design,implement and evaluate satellite system architectural models addressing non-uniform spatiotemporal traffic patterns in particular of handheld services. First, the activity will develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal traffic model, which shall consider available datasets and trend analyses of service requirements of Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and their representative organisations, along with actual and target service coverage obligation set by National Regulation Administrations (NRAs) for terrestrial network gaps. The outputs of this model will be used to define coverage gaps from existing and planned terrestrial networks and space networks. The activity will then study and implement in a software prototype Distributed Satellite System (DSS) concepts for Frequency Range 1 (FR1) considering different orbits, multi-connectivity techniques (e.g. beam overlapping, coordinated multi-point etc) and infrastructure configurations (e.g. fractionated, swarm and federated concepts). System sizing optimizing the satellite resources will be carried out of at least 3 selected DSS concepts and the performance will be evaluated by simulation. The activity shall identify the most promising DSS concept and development roadmap considering complexity and system performance and the ability to accommodateopportunities beyond direct to device services. original.description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. The activity shall establish the required material datasets, perform dedicated measurement and characterisationcampaigns, and integrate the resulting data into an open-access database supporting DQS compliance assessments and brightness prediction tools. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 7.

description: The increasing deployment of satellites is raising concerns regarding their impact on ground- and space-based astronomical observations and the need to comply with emerging Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) requirements. Reliable assessment of spacecraft visibility requires accurate knowledge of the optical properties of external spacecraft materials and their environmental degradation over time. However, existing data are limited, fragmented and often unsuitable for consistent spacecraft-level brightness analyses. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a system-integrated European database of optical properties for spacecraft materials with potential observational impacts, including solar arrays, multilayer insulation, thermo-optical coatings, antennas and external optical elements. The activity shall establish the required material datasets, perform dedicated measurement and characterisationcampaigns, and integrate the resulting data into an open-access database supporting DQS compliance assessments and brightness prediction tools. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 7.
